item.title: A comparison of three models of a whirling string as it becomes chaotic
item.description: arXiv:2611.06567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A stretched wire driven near its fundamental frequency can leave the plane of the driving force and whirl. At larger amplitudes the whirl becomes modulated, reverses its direction, and becomes chaotic. Three models of this motion are in common use: the geometrically exact string equations; a two-mode model -- the Kirchhoff-Carrier equation with one transverse mode in each plane; and the averaged equations for the slow amplitudes of those two modes. We integrate all three under similar conditions and compare them along the route to chaos, which starts with a Hopf bifurcation of the steady whirl and passes through period doublings to chaotic attractors organized by a Shil'nikov homoclinic orbit. The small parameter of the averaging, the ratio $\varepsilon = c/\omega_1$ of the modulation rate to the fundamental frequency, runs from 0.005 to 0.02. Qualitatively the three models agree in the sequence of bifurcations, the coexisting attractors, the return maps and the Lyapunov exponents. Quantitatively, averaging places each local bifurcation $0.7\varepsilon$ to $1.2\varepsilon$ higher in the scaled detuning. The geometrically exact and two-mode models agree with each other to within 0.002 at the local bifurcations for $\varepsilon \le 0.01$. The Shil'nikov ratio, which decides whether chaos accompanies the homoclinic orbit, agrees among the three models to within 1.5% for $\varepsilon \le 0.01$, yet the homoclinic bifurcation itself moves by about $\varepsilon$ at the lower damping and by 6 to 9 times $\varepsilon$ at the higher; the difference is set by how quickly the return of the homoclinic loop changes with detuning.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas B. Tufillaro

item.title: Bypass Transition via the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
item.description: arXiv:2611.05563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Hermitian skin lattices can directionally amplify propagating signals. Here we show that this amplification and nonlinear feedback together drive a bypass transition to self-sustained motion, familiar from shear flows. A finite local excitation can trigger sustained periodic or chaotic motion while the resting state remains linearly stable. We develop a return-map theory that predicts the triggering threshold, its scaling with directional gain, and the instability governing near-critical dynamics. The threshold decreases exponentially with chain length. Weak noise triggers sustained motion as well, with a characteristic ignition length that grows logarithmically as noise weakens at fixed observation time. Our work establishes a skin-effect route to bypass transitions, opening a new avenue for predicting and controlling nonlinear wave dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Konghao Sun, Haiping Hu

item.title: Thermodynamic signatures of the period-doubling route to chemical chaos
item.description: arXiv:2611.06037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chemical reaction networks can evolve from stable oscillations to chaos through successive period doublings. We investigate general properties of entropy-production fluctuations near the onset of chaos and within the chaotic regime in reversible, well-mixed reaction networks. Near an isolated supercritical period-doubling bifurcation, we find a one-sided divergence of the diffusion constant with exponent one. For chaotic attractors satisfying the stated conditions, the entropy variance per unit volume grows exponentially when the macroscopic limit is taken first. Its exponential growth rate is $2\lambda_{\max}$, where $\lambda_{\max}$ is the largest Lyapunov exponent, implying a divergent diffusion constant. We also discuss the volume dependence of the fluctuations and the underlying physical mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Kyota Tamano, Keiji Saito

item.title: Odd Capillarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Capillarity governs interfacial relaxation and hydrodynamic motion in binary fluids through parity-even mechanical stresses. Here, we introduce \emph{odd capillarity}, a parity-breaking interfacial mechanical response, by incorporating a symmetric, nonvariational, parity-odd capillary stress into the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes (CHNS) equations. This stress generates forces along interfaces, transverse to ordinary capillary forces, and performs mechanical work that is not balanced by changes in the composition free energy. Direct numerical simulations reveal that odd capillarity arrests domain coarsening while sustaining turbulent fluid motion without a conventional inertial energy cascade, as energy injection is predominantly balanced by viscous dissipation. In asymmetric mixtures, odd capillarity driven deformation and breakup interrupt droplet growth, producing dynamically arrested emulsions with composition hyperuniformity and suppressed large-scale vorticity fluctuations. These findings establish odd capillarity as a distinct interfacial mechanism for controlling phase separation and sustaining nonequilibrium fluid motion.
item.dc:creator: Nadia Bihari Padhan, Axel Voigt

item.title: Relativistic Quantum Chaos in Neutrino Billiards
item.description: arXiv:2604.13003v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neutrino billiards serve as a model system for the study of aspects of relativistic quantum chaos. These are relativistic quantum billiards consisting of a spin-1/2 particle which is confined to a planar domain by imposing boundary conditions on the spinor components which were proposed in [Berry and Mondragon, {\it Proc. R. Soc.} A {\bf 412}, 53 (1987)]. We review their general features and the properties of neutrino billiards with shapes of billiards with integrable dynamics. Furthermore, we review the features of two neutrino billiards with the shapes of billiards generating a chaotic dynamics, whose nonrelativistic counterpart exhibits particular properties. Finally we briefly discuss possible experimental realizations of relativistic quantum billiards based on graphene billiards, that is, finite-size sheets of graphene.
item.dc:creator: Barbara Dietz

item.title: Stable Ballistic Prograde Cyclers in the Three-Body Problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.29189v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the first continuous families of stable, ballistic, prograde cycler orbits in the circular restricted three-body problem: periodic trajectories that alternately undergo temporary capture and orbit each primary. We construct continuous families of symmetric cyclers from intersections of the stable and unstable manifold tubes of the $L_1$ Lyapunov orbit and exhibit stable examples across more than two orders of magnitude in mass ratio, from the Sun-Jupiter regime to the equal-mass limit. Linear stability separates naturally into planar and out-of-plane components. A planar-stable branch of every computed family is created simultaneously with a hyperbolic branch in a saddle-center bifurcation of the return map at the family's maximal Jacobi constant, while out-of-plane instability occurs only through isolated parametric resonances. Every computed family contains a subfamily that is linearly stable to both planar and out-of-plane perturbations. These stable cyclers persist into the full three-body problem for sufficiently small third mass. We conjecture that saddle-center birth is universal among cycler families, suggesting that stable cyclers are a generic feature of three-body dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Shane D. Ross, Michael Roberts-Tsoukkas

item.title: Butterfly Effects in Turbulence: A Unified View through the Finite Size Lyapunov Exponent
item.description: arXiv:2607.24715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ``butterfly effect'', introduced over half a century ago by Edward Lorenz, has shifted from a cornerstone of dynamical systems to a popular metaphor, yet its true physical manifestation in fully developed turbulence spans a spectrum of phenomena from standard sensitivity on initial conditions to the recently established concept of Eulerian spontaneous stochasticity. Here, we propose an attempt at a systematic synthesis that brings these different but interconnected ideas together within the unifying framework of the Finite Size Lyapunov Exponent (FSLE). The FSLE describes the growth rate of perturbations as a function of their scale, enabling a comprehensive characterization of the multiscale physics of turbulent flows. Using the FSLE and the Sabra shell model, extended to include thermal noise, we bridge the classical, small-scale Lyapunov regime with predictability at large scales and its interpretation in terms of Eulerian spontaneous stochasticity. Moreover, using the FSLE and the Kraichnan model, we also illustrate the closely related phenomenon of Lagrangian spontaneous stochasticity. To complete the spectrum of butterfly effects, we also examine the ``literal butterfly'' scenario of localized, sub-dissipative perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Victor de Jesus Valad\~ao, Erik Aurell, Guido Boffetta, Massimo Cencini, Stefano Musacchio, Angelo Vulpiani

item.title: Bidirectional teleportation using scrambling dynamics: a practical protocol
item.description: arXiv:2601.15536v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic SWAP gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. Our protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill type recovery scheme, associated with the black hole information paradox, with quantum teleportation and runs them in parallel and in opposite directions, enabling bidirectional exchange of quantum states through global interactions alone. This approach cleanly distinguishes the roles of information spreading, entanglement, and chaos for enabling both coherent state transfer and recovery. We propose an experimental realization using the Dicke model, which can be realized in optical cavity and trapped-ion platforms, highlighting the utility of holography in designing practical quantum gates.
item.dc:creator: Amit Vikram, Edwin Chaparro, Muhammad Miskeen Khan, Andrew Lucas, Chris Akers, Ana Maria Rey
